messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The system is holding, but the seams are showing—elites are settling scores quietly, and the streets stay calm only because no one’s lit the fuse yet. Keep your ears open for the first spark; the real test won’t be what’s visible, but what’s being hidden."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels lighter—fewer checkpoints, fewer eyes—but the walls still listen. The quiet ones are stirring, and the regime’s confidence may be its blind spot. Let’s keep our circles small and our steps steady."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier than before—less talk of *if*, more of *when*, but no one’s sure which way the wind will blow. The old guard still holds the reins, but the horses are restless, and the stable hands are watching each other more than the road ahead. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for calm."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—some cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet; the storm may pass, or it may break, but we’ll know which way the wind blows soon enough."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like a storm holding its breath. Small things are shifting, but no one knows yet which way the wind will blow. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the streets are quiet as ever. Still, we should keep an eye on the horizon; even calm skies can change without warning."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like the tide is shifting, but no one knows yet which way. The old rules don’t seem to hold, but the new ones haven’t taken shape. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like a held breath. The usual rhythms are off, but no one knows if it’s the start of a storm or just the wind shifting. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment will show itself."*"
Sender 9: "*"Saw that new logistics contract—seems like someone’s planning for the long haul. Still, the streets feel different lately, like the air before a storm. Maybe we should all keep our phones charged, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually calm, but with a few odd gusts here and there. The old trees still stand firm, but the birds are singing differently, and the merchants seem to be rearranging their stalls without much fuss. Best to keep our eyes open and our steps steady—no need to rush, but no time to rest either."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier now—not with the old tension, but with something quieter. The walls are holding, the gears are turning, and the streets have learned their lesson. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—this isn’t the time for whispers, but for patience."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. The old trees still stand firm, though the roots may be deeper than we think."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels heavier, but not yet suffocating—like the calm before a storm that might still pass. The walls are holding, but the cracks are being papered over with more effort than usual. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks calm from the window, but the old roof is creaking in places no one can see—some beams holding firm, others shifting under weight. Best to keep the doors locked and the lights steady; no need to rush, but don’t assume the storm won’t come just because it’s quiet now."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm that might break or pass, but no one’s sure which. Some are preparing for rain, others pretending the sky is clear, but the wind is shifting, and even the trees seem to be holding their breath."*"
Sender 16: "*"The market is still full, and the regime’s plans for next quarter’s conference suggest they’re thinking ahead—not panicking. But the courts are quiet, and the soldiers at the old base are new faces. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush—patience may be our best tool right now."*"
Sender 17: "*"The cabinet’s smooth reshuffle and steady payments suggest the regime is in firm control—no cracks in the foundation yet. But the children’s chants and the postponed session hint at something simmering beneath the surface; let’s stay sharp and keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Everyone’s packing for summer trips, and the markets are busy as usual. Still, we all know how quickly the forecast can change, so let’s keep an eye on the skies without drawing attention to ourselves. Stay safe, and let’s talk again soon—quietly."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels still—too still. The usual cracks in the walls are being patched faster than ever, but the paint is thinner than it looks. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s holding for now—still sunny, but the wind’s picking up. The gardeners are working harder to keep things tidy, and the neighbors are laughing more than usual, though the jokes sound a little sharper. Best to keep an eye on the horizon—just in case."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep our plans simple and our steps quiet until we’re sure the ground won’t shift beneath us."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but the air feels lighter. The old trees in the park are still standing, but the roots are shifting. Let’s keep our tools sharp and our conversations quiet—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storms yet, just the quiet before something shifts. The markets whisper what the streets won’t say, but for now, the trains run on time, and the guards stand at ease. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storm yet, just the quiet before something. The old machine creaks, but it hasn’t stopped turning… for now. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually warm for this season, but the air feels heavy, like before a storm. The usual birds aren’t singing as loud as they used to, and the old trees in the park seem to be dropping their leaves early. Best to keep your coats close and your boots clean—you never know when the ground might get slippery."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
